title: Why Does an Octopus Have THREE Hearts? 🐙
description:
Why does an octopus have three hearts? Two of them are just for its gills. Its blue blood (blue because it carries oxygen with copper, not iron) squeezes through the gills and comes out at low pressure, all floppy, so heart number three pumps it round the body all over again. You do the same thing: the right side of your heart pumps blood to your lungs, the left side pumps it round your body. Your heart is just two pumps in one box. And when an octopus swims, its hearts stop for a moment (one biologist's best guess: jetting puts so much pressure on them that pausing is easier than pumping), which may be why octopuses would rather crawl. Three hearts or blue blood?
